1902.report: Independent review of PR #1902 (f44e2fd78..f1169ba01) against Issue #1898. The diff is only deploy/acl-hub/** (7 files, +447/-2). Its patch-id (fc24e3b6) is the same as the earlier heads 61c7f3d9c and 1cf7a5664, which was reviewed line by line. Migration 0008 adds users and account_assignments (account_name COLLATE NOCASE, soft removed_at, index on user_email+removed_at) with no proxy or tracking columns. POST /v1/session checks the token with Google tokeninfo. It refuses an unverified email, a domain outside ALLOWED_EMAIL_DOMAINS, an azp/aud other than GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID and a disabled user. Google 5xx or a network failure gives 503 and a rejected token 401. A valid token returns a 30-day key <email>.<exp>.<HMAC-SHA256 USER_KEY_SECRET>. The Google token is never stored (src/users.js:48-76). The user key is parsed from the right, so it is unambiguous; expiry is enforced, the compare is constant-time via sameSecret (src/auth.js:21) and the disabled flag is checked on every request (src/users.js:26-35). GET /v1/my-accounts returns only the caller's rows, including removed ones, with an ETag/304 (src/users.js:79-88). GET /api/users, POST /api/assignments and POST /api/assignments/remove require the owner (OWNER_KEY bearer or the SameSite=Strict owner cookie) or a non-disabled admin user. Without auth they return 401, a buyer gets 403. POST /api/users/role needs OWNER_KEY only (first-admin bootstrap) (src/users.js:164-177). All SQL is parameterized. Assignment rows are allowlisted, so unknown, proxy and tracking fields return 400 with nothing written; the upsert runs in one DB.batch. Remove is a soft update and never deletes. Non-blocking nit: removeAssignments does not check for '@' in user_email (src/users.js:144). Tests: node --test test/users.test.js test/schema.test.js 16/16 pass. The full node --test is 127/130; the same 3 test/report.test.js tests (live levels and text, live filters by manager, object errors are shown as text) fail identically on clean main 1e525327b (time-dependent fixtures), so they are not caused by this PR. Verdict: APPROVED for head 5e801ed2c9ab09ca6ff5e3cfeb9ac9f0969b7051, tree c9f5332478442c12d59292c1f08395ea6eeac3ad, base/main 82d13d826a3c7558196dca2386c3fea5032f6aee. Independent of Worker-W1123A; no source edits or pushes by this reviewer. Lane bed2ee0e271b45dabe2f5205bafd7d8a.

## Diff (3 files)
- src/analysis_agent/morning_service.py: new _drop_hidden_accounts(rows) using hidden_accounts.load()/is_hidden(), called once in the report builder AFTER the sheet rows, the all-CM sheet fallback and the ad_account_map.csv supplement (_fallback_accounts_from_csv) are merged into account_rows. So both the sheet path and the csv path (and the account_rows_cached rebuild path) are filtered. The filtered list is what goes to build_morning_report and report["_account_rows"].
- Key format: Remove (app.py account removal -> hidden_accounts.set_hidden(name, True)) stores the casefolded, whitespace-normalised LABEL only, no country. The builder uses the same is_hidden() with account_label/alias, so it matches Remove exactly. Consequence: Remove hides the label in every country, same as the Accounts page itself (which also unlinks it); a same-named label in another country is the same account label and is hidden too. This differs from ACL-2494's (label, canonical country) keying only because Remove itself is label-keyed; not a defect of this PR.
- Accounts page not affected: /api/accounts-overview reads fetch_account_rows directly (app.py), not the morning report, and hidden state is only read. Side effect (acceptable, noted): report sections built from account_rows also omit removed accounts.
- Restore: /account-map-patch calls set_hidden(name, False); the builder reads the file on each report build, so the account returns on the next build/refresh. Test covers hide then unhide.
- Robustness: load() returns empty set on missing/malformed file; the helper also wraps everything in try/except and returns rows unchanged. Cannot crash the builder.
- hidden_accounts.json is not in the diff (files: changelog.d/ACL-2495.md, morning_service.py, new test). No machine content committed.
- ACL-2494 overlap: main (82d13d826) already contains f4e19635d; git merge-tree of head with current origin/main is clean (tree c9f5332478442c12d59292c1f08395ea6eeac3ad), and the semantic overlap is none: _linked_countries_for/country rows are produced before the filter, and the filter is label-based so it drops all country rows of a removed label, consistent with Remove.

The `src` difference is limited to a removed comment, the order of the copy_more/file_vertical lines in app.py, and an en-dash in a JS comment. tests/test_acl1819_preflight.py adds the new 2-ad-set texts_dynamic parity fixtures. Every note is applied:

- the Primary-text-2 RPA refusal is dropped;
- TermResolver gets cache/scope; API_ONLY_SLOT_KEYS is the union of both sides;
- FUTURE = placements + copyTo; `_targeting_body` is defined once;
- 1774's more_copy_names/vertical_filename are set per ad set.

### Blockers from round 2: fixed
1. **Targeting reads.** `estimate_targeting_reads` = min(90, 6 + 6 × distinct terms and parts across all sets) is added to the per-campaign budget. The write-refusal threshold stays at 250, and the env ceiling is 250+90. I reran my FakeMeta repro (10 sets × 3 ads × 3 work-position terms, cold cache): budget 330, 252 calls used, success. With 4 terms per set the resolver cap is hit and the run is refused before any write ("press Check plan again"); this is 1771 behaviour. 2 sets × 3 terms: success.
2. **ACL-1891.** `_prepare` refuses before the first write when `chunk_calls + estimate_create_calls(plan) > budget`. Check plan (`writing=False`) keeps the old reserve. The 1891 test is rewritten and a new test is added; the 1891 suite passes.

### Non-blocking items from round 2: done
- The pixel guard is dropped.
- Targeting of all ad sets is resolved before one combined TargetingUnresolved is raised.
- A comment now covers creative numbering.
- The changelog covers the v3-page downgrade.

### Remaining notes (non-blocking, no re-review needed)
- **Remaining-budget comment is inaccurate.** The comments say "if writes don't fit after the reads, `_prepare` refuses before the first write". The code only checks when there are large-video chunks. For non-video plans, the targeting reserve is the only guard. One edge: the resolver is shared across campaigns of one job, and its job cap is cumulative (`len(_results)`), so a later campaign can in theory read more than its own reserve. Cheap hardening for a follow-up: an unconditional `client.max_calls - client.calls < estimate_create_calls(plan)` refusal at the end of `_prepare` when writing.
- **The concurrent-confirm test failure is not a lock race.** The 1771 test `test_concurrent_confirms_do_not_lose_entries` (11 == 12 under load) passes in my full group run and in 150 extra 12-thread loops. `ConfirmedStore.put` holds `_STORE_LOCK` around read → modify → atomic replace, so in-process writes are serialized. The likely cause is a transient Windows file-sharing error (AV/indexer) on `os.replace` or `_read`.
  - It does expose a real 1771 robustness gap, so I suggest a follow-up task for 1771 (not this PR):
    - `_read` maps any OSError, including PermissionError, to `{}`, and the next `put` would then rewrite the file with only the new entry, dropping the confirmed cache;
    - `os.replace` is not retried.
  - Fix: on a read error other than file-not-found, refuse to write or retry, and retry the replace on PermissionError.

The write-refusal threshold stays at 250, and the env ceiling is 250+90. I reran my FakeMeta repro (10 sets × 3 ads × 3 work-position terms, cold cache): budget 330, 252 calls used, success. - **Remaining-budget comment is inaccurate.** The comments say "if writes don't fit after the reads, `_prepare` refuses before the first write". The code only checks when there are large-video chunks. For non-video plans, the targeting reserve is the only guard. One edge: the resolver is shared across campaigns of one job, and its job cap is cumulative (`len(_results)`), so a later campaign can in theory read more than its own reserve. Cheap hardening for a follow-up: an unconditional `client.max_calls - client.calls < estimate_create_calls(plan)` refusal at the end of `_prepare` when writing.
- **The concurrent-confirm test failure is not a lock race.** The 1771 test `test_concurrent_confirms_do_not_lose_entries` (11 == 12 under load) passes in my full group run and in 150 extra 12-thread loops. `ConfirmedStore.put` holds `_STORE_LOCK` around read → modify → atomic replace, so in-process writes are serialized. ## Result

Part C of ACL-2091 (parent #1091). Depends on ACL-2548 (#1570), which contains ACL-2547 (#1554). The robot no longer closes the tab that shows a checkpoint, a login page (page evidence) or a Meta policy block: `PageTab.leave_open()` only ends our CDP connection. Warm path: `_note_login_stop` / `_finish` leave the tab, keep `target_id` (protected by `known_targets()`), set `stale_target` for the next good checkout, and record the kind so the chip says "Security check" for a checkpoint. Cold read and cold publish do the same. Frozen tabs and token-only logouts are still dropped. A job that ends on such a problem keeps the profile window whatever `ACL_KEEP_PROFILES_OPEN` says (`finish_job` returns `kept_problem`), holds a `review` slot and sets `job["profile_problem"]` (kind, reason, next step) from the Part A texts. A profile closed on purpose by the auto resume (ACL-2345) is not kept. `ProfileSlots.resolve_kept` moves a solved review window to `convenience`.
